message.content:
**Gini coefficient of the United States (most recent estimate)**  
- **2022 (U.S. Census Bureau)**: **≈ 41.5**  
- **2019 (OECD & World Bank)**: **≈ 41.4**

> *The Gini coefficient is a single‑number summary of income inequality, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) to 100 (perfect inequality). A value of 41.5 indicates that the U.S. has relatively high income inequality compared with many other OECD countries (e.g., Canada ≈ 33.3, Germany ≈ 31.9, Japan ≈ 32.5).*

### Sources
| Source | Year | Value | Link |
|--------|------|-------|------|
| U.S. Census Bureau – Income Inequality | 2022 | 41.5 | https://www.census.gov/data/tables/2022/demo/income-poverty/income-inequality.html |
| OECD – Income Inequality | 2019 | 41.4 | https://data.oecd.org/inequality/gini-index.htm |
| World Bank – Gini Index | 2019 | 41.4 | https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SI.POV.GINI |

> **Note:** Different agencies use slightly different methodologies (e.g., household surveys vs. tax records), so the exact figure can vary by a few tenths. The 2022 Census estimate is the most recent publicly available figure for the U.S. at the time of writing.
